sourcePixelSection:
Opened the complete actual bookroot PNG alone before the other eight images or any page prose.

Path: `ssot-resources/soviet10year-textbooks/artifacts/10c/figures/fig-12.png`.
SHA256: `a5970d8c13709475dcfd0fec39a8730bdf595686c2d8218e307b19e3507648a7`.

- One wide Cartesian frame, no panel division or grid. Horizontal solid axis extends far left and has a rightward arrow and x label; vertical solid axis has an upward arrow and y label, extends below the negative unit level, and crosses the horizontal axis near the middle-left.
- y-axis has original +1 and -1 level ticks/text. x-axis has the printed -pi/4 location left of the vertical axis. The oval printed immediately lower-right of the axes crossing is `ROUND-GLYPH-UNKNOWN`, not a recovered codepoint.
- Two full visible periodic curves have equal vertical excursion: heavy SOLID curve and thinner DASHED curve. Both show repeated positive crests/negative troughs above/below the x-axis, with the solid ahead of the dashed horizontally; they overlap/cross between corresponding crest/trough portions. Each retains its actual finite crop endpoints, without inventing endpoint dots, continuation arrows, or a numerical domain from the canvas edge.
- The heavy solid curve crosses the negative-side x location labelled -pi/4 while rising, and is already positive at the vertical axis. The dashed curve crosses the axes vicinity rising. The solid and dashed crests to the right of the vertical axis are offset, as are the later troughs and next crests; both are visible through a right descending portion. No crossing point is named or dotted.
- The printed `y = sin x` formula has a slanted arrowed leader pointing to the DASHED curve around its first positive crest/right shoulder. The printed `y = sin(x + pi/4)` formula has a separate curved/down-right arrowed leader to the rising SOLID curve on the right. Both exact formula roles, leader attachment and solid/dash distinctions must survive; a generic wave or swapped labels would change source content.
- Only the original labelled unit levels and phase tick are numerical scale facts. Small axis-ink irregularities are not a recovered regularly numbered tick lattice. Finite endpoint abscissae and unlabelled individual extrema/crossing coordinates are not exactly recoverable from this ungridded crop alone; the later faithful stated formula supplies functional relationships, not permission to extend the visible domain.

Required later executable coverage: shared axes/scales, the phase tick, both formula/leader attachments, exact source-bound curve identities and relative phase, visible roots/extrema/curve crossings over the retained interval, and individual solid/dashed roles. This is a requirements inventory, not a drafted spec.
